title: Microsoft Licensing Cost Governance — EA, CSP & True-Up Readiness
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (governance across Microsoft EA/CSP agreements, true-up management, cost modeling; multi-stakeholder, higher risk to spend/compliance).
hook: Govern Microsoft licensing across EA and CSP — and never fear a true-up again
problem: Microsoft licensing is a moving target: an Enterprise Agreement here, CSP subscriptions there, annual true-ups, and renewals that arrive with surprises. Without governance you over-buy to be safe or under-license and risk a shortfall. This solution establishes Microsoft licensing cost governance across EA and CSP — a clear model of what you own under each agreement, true-up readiness, renewal planning, and the cost controls to right-size commitments with confidence.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the EA vs. CSP models, how true-ups work, the cost-governance cadence, and how entitlement counts map to deployment and growth.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Entra ID, admin/billing access, EA/CSP agreement details, usage/deployment data, procurement alignment) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: inventory agreements and entitlements, map deployment/growth, model true-up exposure, set renewal and right-sizing decisions, establish a governance cadence and KPIs, then pilot, validate, and expand.
5 PowerShell scripts — entitlement/assignment discovery, true-up-exposure validation, a license position and cost report, safe remediation of mis-assignments, and a governance-scope group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: Establish Microsoft licensing cost governance across EA and CSP — a clear model of what you own, true-up readiness, renewal planning, and cost controls to right-size commitments. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
